style: Say in a relaxed, friendly way, like a kind dad helping with homework. A retired local news producer mentoring a high-school crew.
lines: Drag Release forms onto a day first. Then drag the shoots onto days that work.
Select a shoot card, then tap an open calendar slot. Tap a placed shoot to remove it.
Tap Fill in to cover that role yourself.
Everything's scheduled. Tap Wrap shooting to see your footage.
Drag clips onto the timeline. Aim for about five minutes.
Select a clip in the bin and tap Add to end. Select a timeline clip to change it.
No footage was shot. Tap Start over to return to the calendar.
Long talking heads lose people. Tap the clip, then tap Cover to lay footage over it.
Tap Screen it and watch the line under your cut.
Tap Screen it to test this cut, or Back to Edit to change it.
Watch the audience line. Tap Stop to interrupt the screening.
Tap Back to Edit to fix the highlighted lowest point.
They stayed with you the whole way, and nobody was confused.
Choose Where and Captions. Fill the title, date, Invite and Who should see this fields.
Your plan is complete. Tap Lock the plan to make the final sheet.
Your premiere sheet is ready. Tap Print sheet to keep a copy.
Set the in and out seconds, then tap Apply. Keep at least three seconds.
Choose B-roll, then its cover length. Tap Apply to cover the interview's last seconds.
Type the speaker's name and role, then tap Apply.
Type the archive date and place, then tap Apply.
Read the model, then tap Close to return to your screening.
Tap Wrap anyway to finish without these shoots, or Cancel to return to the calendar.
Tap Start over to clear this documentary, or Cancel to keep it.
Ruiz Shoe Repair has been on Main Street since 1962. Ana Ruiz, seventy one, runs it alone and plans to close next spring.
Your crew has three weeks to shoot and one week to cut a five minute documentary for the town. Tap Close to return to the calendar.
